analyzed_vuln.description: `idprime_get_token_name()` allocates `*tname` and, on `read_binary` short/failed read (`r < 1`), frees that buffer but does not null out `*tname` and returns an error. The caller path in `sc_pkcs15emu_idprime_init()` keeps the `token_name` pointer variable and later cleanup (`sc_pkcs15_clear_tokeninfo` via card free) frees the same pointer again after it has been assigned into `p15card->tokeninfo->label`, causing a double-free. Root cause is ownership/lifetime violation in `idprime_get_token_name` error handling (freeing caller-owned out-pointer without resetting it).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In fuzz_pkcs15_reader, `sc_pkcs15_bind` reaches IDPrime emulation (`sc_pkcs15emu_idprime_init`), which calls `sc_card_ctl(...SC_CARDCTL_IDPRIME_GET_TOKEN_NAME...)` -> `idprime_get_token_name`. Input/card state must make token-info file appear present and pass initial checks, allocate token name, then make second `read_binary` return `<1` so `idprime_get_token_name` frees the allocated buffer and returns error with stale pointer. Later teardown (`sc_pkcs15_card_free` -> `sc_pkcs15_clear_tokeninfo`) frees `tokeninfo->label` that aliases that stale pointer, triggering double-free.
